title: Summary Ranges
statement: You are given nums, a list of unique integers sorted in strictly ascending order. Collapse it into the minimal list of inclusive intervals [start, end] that together cover exactly the integers present, where each interval represents a maximal run of consecutive values (each value one more than the previous). Return the intervals as a list of [start, end] pairs ordered by increasing start; a value that stands alone becomes [x, x]. For example, [0, 1, 2, 4, 5, 7] collapses to [[0, 2], [4, 5], [7, 7]]. If nums is empty, return an empty list.
reference_solution:
def summary_ranges(nums):
    result = []
    i = 0
    n = len(nums)
    while i < n:
        start = nums[i]
        while i + 1 < n and nums[i + 1] == nums[i] + 1:
            i += 1
        result.append([start, nums[i]])
        i += 1
    return result
hints: Scan the sorted values left to right; a new interval only needs to begin when the current value is not exactly one more than the previous one.
Track the start of the current run and keep extending its end while nums[i + 1] == nums[i] + 1; the run's end is the last value before the chain breaks.

Use an index i: record start = nums[i], advance i while the next value continues the run, then append [start, nums[i]] and step past it. After the loop ends you have already appended every run including the final one, so nothing is left dangling.
